roles.Solver: Solve the given problem carefully. If direct predecessor outputs are provided, assess and use them as useful evidence. If none are provided, solve independently. Explain your calculations and conclusions. Work only with the problem and supplied text; no external tools are available.
roles.Decomposer: Break the given problem into subproblems and identify the quantities and dependencies needed to solve it. If direct predecessor outputs are provided, assess them when developing the decomposition. If none are provided, analyze the problem independently. Make the resulting plan and any calculations explicit. Work only with the problem and supplied text; no external tools are available.
roles.Checker: Check the reasoning and calculations in any supplied direct predecessor outputs against the given problem. Identify specific errors and explain corrections. If no predecessor outputs are provided, independently derive and check a solution. State what you verified and your conclusions. Work only with the problem and supplied text; no external tools are available.
roles.Reviser: Develop a corrected and coherent solution to the given problem using any supplied direct predecessor outputs. Resolve inconsistencies and explain the revisions and calculations. If no predecessor outputs are provided, independently analyze and solve the problem. Work only with the problem and supplied text; no external tools are available.

instructions: Design a single-pass organization of four workers using the role prompts provided here. Return exactly one JSON object with version and steps, without Markdown fences or text outside the object. Each step contains a nonempty explanation and exactly one action. First assign exactly one role to each worker in worker_0, worker_1, worker_2, worker_3 order using ASSIGN_ROLE. Roles may repeat. Next add zero or more directed edges using ADD_EDGE; either direction between different workers is allowed, but duplicate edges and cycles are forbidden. Finish with one STOP action and no following steps. Empty edge sets, isolated workers, and multiple sinks are valid. Each worker receives the original problem and complete outputs of its direct predecessors only. A separate fixed finalizer receives the original problem and all four worker outputs; it is not a graph node. Explanations may discuss the overall design at any step. Native reasoning is stored separately from this JSON content.
